books.IF: Introduction to Flight, 9th ed. — John D. Anderson Jr. & Mary L. Bowden
books.PHAK: Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge (FAA-H-8083-25) — FAA
books.SSF: The Simple Science of Flight: From Insects to Jumbo Jets — Henk Tennekes
books.UF: Understanding Flight — David F. Anderson & Scott Eberhardt
books.K360: Kokpit 360 trivia style (practical 'why is the plane like this?' facts)

how_to_use: The user's rule since 2026-11-23: every Kokpit 360 topic comes from this bank (built from the user's 5 sources). Pick ONE topic without used_by; prefer priority 1, never two in a row from the same series, and respect 'avoid_overlap'. Build the script from its hook + max 3 facts. The facts are the books' claims: STILL confirm every number with web search (2 reliable sources, e.g. NASA Glenn, FAA, Boeing/Airbus, SKYbrary, university pages) and cut what you can't confirm. Put the book (full name) + the web sources in script.json 'sources'. Never quote the books' wording; say it in your own Turkish. After the video is made, set used_by=<slug> and commit this file to engine/ with the video. When fewer than 5 unused topics remain, tell the user and suggest new ones from the same books.
accuracy_notes: LIFT: do not say 'Bernoulli is wrong'. Bernoulli's pressure-speed relation is correct; what is wrong is the 'equal transit time' story. The pressure difference and the downwash are two descriptions of the same force (IF: pressure is the cause; UF/SSF: think of it as pushing air down). Say 'okulda öğretilen hikâye eksik', not 'fizik yanlış'.
Coanda: present the spoon/glass under a tap as an ANALOGY for flow following a curved surface, not as the full scientific cause of lift (aerodynamicists dispute that).
Altimeter 29.92 / 1013: 18,000 ft is the USA transition altitude; in Türkiye and Europe it is lower and set per airport. Say that if the topic uses it.
Hypoxia: calm, practical, no fear; never tie it to a real accident.
No crash exploitation (PLAYBOOK 3): no real accident footage, victims or tragedy hooks.

topics.title_tr: Kanat nasıl uçar? Okuldaki hikâye eksik
topics.hook: Okulda kanadın altındaki ve üstündeki hava aynı anda buluşur dediler… ama üstteki hava çok daha önce varıyor.
facts: The 'equal transit time' idea is false (UF, SSF).
Simulations / wind tunnel smoke show the air over the top reaches the trailing edge well BEFORE the air underneath (UF).
Lift = the wing turning air downward (downwash); the low pressure on top is what bends and speeds the air, not the other way round (UF, SSF).
topics.visual: airfoil in wind tunnel, two smoke pulses split at the leading edge, top pulse races ahead; then a downwash arrow sheet behind the wing
topics.verify: NASA Glenn 'incorrect lift theory equal transit'; Cambridge Univ. Holger Babinsky lift video

topics.hook: Kanat üstü kavisli diye uçuyorsa… ters dönen uçak neden düşmüyor?
facts: Aerobatic planes often use symmetric airfoils (same curve top and bottom) (UF).
What makes lift is the angle of attack: tilt the wing and it pushes air down either way up (UF).
Upside down the pilot simply pushes the nose 'up' relative to the ground to keep a positive angle of attack (UF).
topics.visual: symmetric airfoil rotating 180°, angle-of-attack arc and downwash arrows appear in both orientations; aerobatic plane flips over clouds
topics.verify: NASA Glenn 'inclination effects on lift'; FAA aerobatic/airfoil references

topics.hook: Alçaktan geçen bir jet sis tabakasında koca bir delik bırakır… ama ona hiç dokunmaz.
facts: A wing works by pushing a huge mass of air down (downwash) (UF).
A low-flying aircraft over fog/cloud tops leaves a visible trough from that downwash (UF).
Newton's third law: push air down, the air pushes the plane up (UF, PHAK).
topics.visual: airliner skimming a flat cloud deck, a channel sinks open behind it; force arrows down/up
topics.verify: search 'aircraft downwash cloud hole photo' (fallstreak/wake trough pictures); NASA Glenn Newton's third law lift

topics.hook: Kanadın ucu boşuna kıvrık değil… orada gizli bir kasırga dönüyor.
facts: High-pressure air under the wing spills around the tip into the low-pressure top, forming a wingtip vortex (PHAK, SSF).
That vortex costs energy: induced drag (PHAK, IF).
Winglets / longer spans weaken it — fuel saving of a few percent per flight (SSF; confirm %: Boeing/NASA give ~4-6 %).
topics.visual: wing with streamlines curling into a spiral tube at the tip; winglet folds up and the spiral shrinks
topics.verify: NASA 'winglets' fact sheet (Whitcomb); Boeing Aero magazine blended winglets fuel savings

topics.title_tr: Planörlerin kanadı neden bu kadar uzun?
topics.hook: Motoru yok… ama bir kilometre yükseklikten altmış kilometre süzülebiliyor.
facts: Top sailplanes reach glide ratios around 60:1 (UF).
Long, slender wings = high aspect ratio (span²/area), which cuts induced drag (IF, SSF).
Same idea made the U-2 spy plane's wings long for endurance (IF).
topics.visual: slender sailplane over valley, glide-slope line with 1 km down / 60 km forward ruler; aspect-ratio comparison of two wing outlines
topics.verify: glide ratio of open-class sailplanes (e.g. eta, ASH 31) ≥ 60; NASA aspect ratio page

topics.title_tr: Motorlar dursa yolcu uçağı ne kadar süzülür?
topics.hook: İki motor birden sussa uçak taş gibi düşer mi? Hayır… yüz kilometreden fazla süzülür.
facts: Glide 'finesse' = lift/drag = metres forward per metre of height lost (SSF).
A jet airliner has L/D ≈ 15-20 (SSF; verify for 747/A320).
From 10-11 km cruise height that is roughly 150-200 km of glide in still air (compute from the verified L/D).
topics.visual: airliner over clouds, engines' glow fades, long dashed glide line with altitude and distance counters
topics.verify: airliner lift-to-drag ratio sources (Boeing, Airbus, university notes); do NOT name real accidents

topics.hook: Uçak direksiyonla döner sanırsın… ama pilot dönerken ayağıyla da bastırmak zorunda.
facts: Ailerons roll the plane: one goes down (more lift), one goes up (PHAK).
The rising wing also gets more induced drag, so the nose swings the WRONG way: adverse yaw (PHAK, UF).
The rudder pedals cancel it — that is a coordinated turn; designers also use differential/Frise ailerons (PHAK).
topics.visual: top-down plane rolling right while nose yaws left (red arc), rudder deflects and arc turns green; pedals close-up
topics.verify: FAA PHAK chapter 6 adverse yaw; SKYbrary adverse yaw

topics.hook: Bir uçağı sadece üç hareket uçurur… ve her biri ayrı bir parçada saklı.
facts: Roll around the longitudinal axis — ailerons (PHAK).
Pitch around the lateral axis — elevator (PHAK).
Yaw around the vertical axis — rudder; all three cross at the centre of gravity (PHAK, UF).
topics.visual: 3 glowing axis lines through the CG, each surface lights up as the plane rotates on its axis
topics.verify: FAA PHAK ch.5/6 axes of an aircraft; NASA Glenn 'aircraft rotations'

topics.hook: Önden bak, kanatlar hafif yukarı kalkık… bu küçük açı uçağı kendi kendine düzeltir.
facts: The upward V angle is called dihedral (PHAK).
When a gust drops one wing, the plane slips toward it and the lower wing meets the air at a bigger angle, gets more lift and rises back (PHAK).
That built-in roll stability means the plane tends to level itself (PHAK).
topics.visual: front view of airliner, gust tips it, side-slip arrows, low wing lift arrow grows, plane rights itself
topics.verify: FAA PHAK dihedral lateral stability; NASA Glenn dihedral

topics.hook: Kuyruktaki küçük kanat uçağı kaldırır sanırsın… ama aslında aşağı bastırıyor.
facts: The centre of gravity sits ahead of the centre of lift, so the plane naturally wants to pitch nose-down (PHAK).
The horizontal tail makes a small DOWNWARD force to balance it, like a seesaw (PHAK).
Result: a nose-heavy plane that recovers on its own if it slows — stable by design (PHAK, IF).
topics.visual: side view seesaw: CG ball ahead of lift arrow, nose tips down, tail arrow pushes down and it balances; seesaw graphic overlay
topics.verify: FAA PHAK longitudinal stability, tail-down force

topics.title_tr: Jet motoru itişin çoğunu nereden alır?
topics.hook: Jet motoru arkadan ateş püskürterek iter sanırsın… ama asıl işi öndeki dev pervane yapar.
facts: In a high-bypass turbofan most air goes AROUND the hot core (bypass air) (IF, UF).
That fan makes most of the thrust (verify: ~80 % or more on modern engines).
Pushing a lot of air a little is more efficient than a little air a lot: TSFC ~0.6 vs ~1.0 for a pure turbojet (IF).
topics.visual: reuse turbofan(E) cutaway: cold blue bypass stream vs thin orange core stream, a % bar fills
topics.verify: GE/Rolls-Royce or NASA Glenn turbofan bypass ratio; TSFC values
topics.avoid_overlap: kokpit-jetmotor (earlier video was why the engine doesn't melt; this angle is thrust — say 'motorun bir başka sırrı')

topics.title_tr: Sinek ve Boeing 747 aynı kurala uyar
topics.hook: Bir sinek ile bir jumbo jet aynı kuralla uçar… ve bu kural 747'yi sadece iki yüz kat hızlı yapar.
facts: Tennekes plots insects, birds and airliners on one 'Great Flight Diagram' (SSF).
A 747 is about 500 billion times heavier than a fruit fly (SSF).
But it cruises only ~200 times faster: wing loading grows with size, so bigger flyers must fly faster (W/S ∝ W^1/3) (SSF).
topics.visual: tiny fly next to a 747 on a log scale; weight counter shoots up, speed counter barely moves
topics.verify: Tennekes Great Flight Diagram (MIT Press page/reviews); fruit fly ~1 mg & 747 ~400 t masses, cruise speeds

topics.hook: Kuşlar havada durur gibi süzülür… ama bir jumbo jet yavaşlarsa düşer.
facts: Wing loading = weight per wing area: insects ~1-10, birds ~10-100, airliners thousands of N/m² (UF).
Higher wing loading needs higher speed to make enough lift (SSF, UF).
That's why big jets need flaps and long runways for take-off and landing (PHAK).
topics.visual: bar chart insect/bird/plane on log bars; then airliner extending flaps on approach
topics.verify: wing loading values for a sparrow/starling and a 747/A380

topics.title_tr: Bütün yolcu uçakları neden birbirine benzer?
topics.hook: Boeing ile Airbus rakip… ama uçakları neredeyse ikiz gibi.
facts: Long-range jets (747, 777, A340) converged on similar weights, wing loadings and cruise speeds (SSF).
Cruise speed sits just below the speed of sound, where drag rises sharply (SSF, IF).
Physics, not copying, sets the shape: swept wings, under-wing engines, tube fuselage (SSF).
topics.visual: three generic silhouettes morph into one; Mach 0.85 gauge
topics.verify: cruise Mach of 777/A350/747 (~0.84-0.86); wing loading figures
topics.note: Use generic shapes only — no airline liveries or logos.

topics.hook: İnsanlığın ilk motorlu uçuşu… bugünkü bir uçağın kabininde bitebilirdi.
facts: 17 Dec 1903: the Wright Flyer flew about 36.5 m (120 ft) in 12 s (IF).
A Boeing 777-300 is about 74 m long — the first flight is less than half of it (UF).
It flew at ~30 mph ground speed; today's jets cruise ~900 km/h (IF).
topics.visual: 777 silhouette on a runway, a tiny biplane flies along its body and lands before the wing root; distance ruler
topics.verify: Smithsonian NASM first flight distance; Boeing 777-300 length

topics.hook: Ses hızını geçen uçağın önünde görünmez bir duvar oluşur… ve sivri burun onu keser.
facts: Above Mach 1, pressure 'warnings' can't travel ahead, so air piles up into thin shock waves (UF, IF).
Shocks bring a big extra drag: wave drag (PHAK, IF).
A sharp nose and thin edges make a slanted (oblique) shock instead of a blunt wall, cutting that drag (UF).
topics.visual: blunt body with a thick bow shock vs needle nose with thin swept shock cone; Mach gauge passes 1
topics.verify: NASA Glenn oblique shock / wave drag

topics.hook: Pilot 'stall' dediğinde motor durdu sanırsın… ama motorla hiç ilgisi yok.
facts: A stall is the WING losing lift, not the engine (PHAK).
It happens when the angle of attack gets too steep (typically ~15-18° for many airfoils; verify) (PHAK, IF).
The air layer on the wing (boundary layer) runs out of energy and peels off: flow separation (IF, PHAK).
topics.visual: airfoil tilting up, smooth streamlines turn into swirling separated flow on top; lift arrow shrinks; engine keeps spinning (green)
topics.verify: FAA PHAK stall/critical AoA; SKYbrary stall

topics.title_tr: Sıcak havada uçak neden zor kalkar?
topics.hook: Aynı uçak, aynı pist… ama yazın kalkmak için çok daha uzun koşar.
facts: Warm air is less dense: pilots call this high density altitude (PHAK).
Thinner air = less lift, less engine power, less propeller bite (PHAK).
So hot, high airports need longer take-off runs and sometimes less weight (PHAK; verify an example with numbers).
topics.visual: same plane on two runways, summer sun vs winter; air molecules sparse vs dense; take-off distance bars
topics.verify: FAA density altitude pamphlet; an example hot/high airport
topics.note: Strong Türkiye trigger in summer; fine any time.

topics.title_tr: Maske düşerse neden önce kendine takarsın?
topics.hook: Uçakta maske düşerse önce çocuğuna değil, kendine takarsın… çünkü saniyelerin var.
facts: At ~35,000 ft without oxygen the time of useful consciousness is about 30-60 s (PHAK).
Hypoxia feels pleasant at first (euphoria) and dulls judgement, so people don't notice it (PHAK).
Hence: own mask first, then help others (verify with airline/FAA safety guidance).
topics.visual: cabin cutaway, mask drops, big countdown 60→30 s ring, altitude gauge 35,000 ft
topics.verify: FAA AC 61-107 / FAA hypoxia brochure TUC table
topics.note: Calm, practical tone; no fear, no accidents.

topics.title_tr: Uçak gövdesi bir yumurta kabuğu gibi
topics.hook: Uçağın gövdesi sadece bir kabuk değil… içinde görünmez bir iskelet var.
facts: Monocoque = the skin carries all the load, like an egg — light but dents buckle it (PHAK).
Airliners use semimonocoque: frames (formers), bulkheads and long stringers back the skin (PHAK).
That lets the cabin hold pressure flight after flight (PHAK; verify cabin pressure differential ~8 psi).
topics.visual: fuselage cutaway peels the skin to show rings and stringers; pressure arrows push outward
topics.verify: FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook – Airframe ch.1 structures
topics.avoid_overlap: kokpit-pencere-delik (pressure was covered; focus on the skeleton)

topics.hook: İnişte kanadın içinden yeni kanatlar çıkar… çünkü uçak yavaşlarken düşmemeli.
facts: Flaps (rear) and slats (front) extend to add camber and area (PHAK).
More lift at low speed, so the plane can land slower and shorter (PHAK, IF).
The price is extra drag — useful on approach, wasted in cruise, so they retract (PHAK).
topics.visual: wing cross-section slides open: slat forward, flap back and down; speed gauge drops, lift arrow holds
topics.verify: FAA PHAK ch.6 flaps and leading edge devices; Boeing/Airbus approach speeds

topics.hook: Kuyrukta avuç içi kadar bir parça var… ve koca dümeni o hareket ettirir.
facts: Trim tabs are small surfaces on the trailing edge of a control surface (PHAK).
Moving the tab one way pushes the big surface the other way with airflow (PHAK).
So the pilot doesn't have to hold the yoke for hours (PHAK).
topics.visual: elevator close-up, tiny tab tilts down and the whole elevator swings up; yoke force meter drops to zero
topics.verify: FAA PHAK trim tabs

topics.hook: Bir savaş uçağı motoru kıssa bile… sadece hızıyla üç kilometre tırmanabilir.
facts: Energy height h_e = h + V²/2g puts speed and height in one number (IF).
At 250 m/s, V²/2g ≈ 3,190 m of 'stored' climb (compute in code).
Pilots trade speed for height and back like a roller coaster (IF).
topics.visual: jet zooms up a dotted parabola while a speed bar drains into an altitude bar; roller-coaster overlay
topics.verify: energy height / specific energy definition (NASA/FAA or university notes); compute the number in python

topics.hook: İnişte uçak yere değmek istemiyormuş gibi süzülür… bunun adı yer etkisi.
facts: Within about one wingspan of the ground the wingtip vortices and downwash are squashed (UF, PHAK).
Less induced drag → the plane floats further than expected (PHAK).
Pilots plan for it on landing; some birds skim water for the same reason (UF, SSF).
topics.visual: wing near runway: vortex spirals flatten; plane floats along the centreline; pelican skimming water inset
topics.verify: FAA PHAK ground effect; SKYbrary ground effect

topics.title_tr: Uçak yavaşlamak için daha çok güç ister
topics.hook: Arabada yavaşlamak için gazı bırakırsın… ama uçak çok yavaşlayınca daha fazla gaz ister.
facts: At low speed the wing needs a high angle of attack, which means much more induced drag (UF, SSF).
Below a certain speed the power needed goes UP as you slow: 'backside of the power curve' (UF).
That's why slow flight near landing is demanding (UF, PHAK).
topics.visual: U-shaped power curve graph drawn live, dot slides left and climbs; plane nose-high
topics.verify: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook region of reversed command

topics.hook: Wright kardeşlerden elli yıl önce bir planör bir adamı vadinin üstünden uçurdu.
facts: Sir George Cayley's 1853 glider carried a person across Brompton Dale (IF; verify).
Its wing had an aspect ratio near 1 and L/D about 3 (IF).
Modern gliders exceed 40-60: same physics, far better wings (IF, UF).
topics.visual: wooden 19th-century glider over a valley in paper-sketch shading, then morphs into a slender sailplane; L/D counter 3 → 60
topics.verify: Cayley 1853 coachman flight (Smithsonian/RAeS); Anderson L/D 3.08 figure
